focus_areas: Geometric separation between bison and background (depth/occlusion)
Topological integrity of hooves against the gravel ground
Fur texture transition (shaggy forequarters to smooth hindquarters)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the contact points between the hooves and the gravel; ensure there is no 'melting' or blurring that suggests the legs are merging with the ground. Verify the depth relationship between the main bison and the background herd—the background animals should be clearly further away and not bleeding into the foreground subject. Check the background bison for any signs of structural collapse or unnatural distortion.
image_description: A full-body side profile of an American Bison standing on a gravel path. The bison features a massive, dark brown shaggy coat covering the head, neck, and forequarters, forming a distinct shoulder hump. The hindquarters are less furred with shorter hair. It has short, curved horns, a beard under the chin, and sturdy legs ending in hooves. In the background, other bison are visible grazing in a green field.
